question: How should the app that uses the table tell it which look to use? ZestTabs just follows a 'dark' class that the app puts on the page (body.dark) and has no setting of its own. For the table, do you want that same approach, a setting you pass to the table (for example theme="dark" | "light" | "system"), or both?
optionLabel: Both: a theme setting on the table, and when it is not given the table follows body.dark like ZestTabs

The app that uses the table controls it: an optional `theme` prop ('light' | 'dark' | 'system') on the table, and when the prop is not given the table follows the `dark` class on the page body (body.dark), the same convention ZestTabs uses. Existing apps see no change unless they opt in. Every part of the table (desktop view, mobile cards, header, rows, detail rows, skeleton, spinner, empty and no-more-data messages, filter and selection controls) follows the active theme through CSS variables.

In the responsive table's mobile card layout, move each card's expand/collapse chevron row from the top of the card to the bottom, after the card's data rows and directly above the detail panel it opens. The chevron row stays left-aligned as it is today. The desktop table layout, the chevron's existing behaviour and the detail panel's content stay unchanged. This puts the expand control next to the content it reveals, as the developer asked.

What will be built:

1. R1: In mobile card view, each card's expand/collapse chevron row appears at the bottom of the card, after all of the card's data rows, instead of before them at the top. The row stays left-aligned within the card as it is today; it does not become a full-width footer bar.
   Done when:
   • On a mobile viewport, the chevron row is rendered below every data row inside the card and not above the first data row.
   • …and 3 more

2. R2: The mobile chevron row's spacing and separator reflect its new position as the last row of the card: the separator that currently sits below the chevron row and the bottom margin that assumed a top row are removed or moved to the top edge of the row.
   Done when:
   • The chevron row no longer has a bottom border or bottom margin that separates it from the card body.
   • …and 1 more

3. R3: Expanding a mobile card still opens its detail panel immediately below that card, with the chevron row directly above the panel.
   Done when:
   • With a card collapsed, no detail panel is visible; with it expanded, the panel appears below the card.
   • …and 2 more

4. R4: Desktop view is unchanged: its expand/collapse chevron remains in the first column of the table row, not at the bottom of a card.
   Done when:
   • On a desktop viewport, the chevron appears in the first column of the row as it did before.
   • …and 1 more

5. R5: The documentation that describes the mobile chevron as a top-of-card row is updated to describe it as a bottom-of-card row.
   Done when:
   • The documentation no longer describes the mobile chevron row as being at the top of the card.
   • …and 1 more

Assumed for you (tell me if any is wrong):

1. The chevron row keeps its existing icon, keyboard handling and aria-expanded behaviour; only its vertical position and separator styling change.
2. A card may contain any number of data rows; the chevron row always follows the last one.
3. The detail panel continues to render outside and after the card, as it does today.

Not included:

• Changing the chevron icon, colour, size or horizontal alignment
• Changing the content, animation or chrome of the detail panel
• Changing the desktop table layout
• Changing which rows are expandable or what data a card shows

question:
Before anything is built, DevTeam found instructions that cannot all be followed. Think of two people, Alice and Bob, who were each told something different.
Alice is R5, what you asked for. Bob is the check TEST-001. The design's only test component covers R1, R2, R3, R4 and A1, and docs/expand-collapse.md is listed separately with R5 and no test, so no automated test names R5 and TEST-001 ('every requirement is proven by at least one test that names it') fails as the plan stands. A doc-assertion test in the new test file would fix it without changing any requirement.
Alice is R2, what you asked for. Bob is the design (design). R2's second acceptance line is a visual judgement ('reads visually as the last row') that no automated test can prove; the design's substitute is a CSS contract test that only asserts the presence of border-top/margin-top in the text of the module.css file (CSS values cannot be read through computed styles because CSS is mapped to identity-obj-proxy), so QA could never accept that line on evidence. The acceptance line needs rewording to something provable (e.g. the row has border-top/margin-top and its top border is adjacent to the last data row), or the requirement must say how it is accepted.
Nothing done so far is thrown away. How should it be settled?
optionLabel: Keep the requirement, and relax TEST-001 for this feature
